prompt: Write a method that repeats a word n times with a separator between copies. Complete the repeatJoin method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Concatenating strings with + inside a loop creates a new String object every iteration; a StringBuilder appends into one growing buffer instead, which is the idiomatic (and much faster) approach. The separator-between-items pattern -- append sep only when i > 0 -- puts sep between copies without adding one at either end. With n = 0 the loop body never runs and the empty builder naturally yields "".
hints: Use a StringBuilder and a loop that runs n times, appending word each pass.
To get sep BETWEEN copies only, append sep before word whenever i > 0.
n = 0 needs no special case -- the loop simply never runs and the builder is empty.
